title: Bound and authenticate overall-goal summarization
description:
The daemon-wide overall-goal summarizer launched hundreds of unauthenticated Grok processes for incorrectly correlated histories, causing an xAI browser-tab flood and Chrome failure. Harden selection, authentication, retry limits, concurrency, observability, and validation before arcmux may restart.

2026-07-30 sustainable-fix scope: eliminate daemon-side agent CLI execution from both automatic and POST /session/summarize paths; use only explicit direct API providers; persist bounded per-turn retry state; consume only the frontmatter-verified canonical_history binding; and make installed-artifact safety verifiable before restart. Production remains inactive and disabled during implementation.
design: Use turn_contract.canonical_history (hook.canonical_history_frontmatter.v1), not legacy vault_link, as the only transcript identity. Resolve the exact regular non-symlink history file under the configured history root and reverify its conversation_id before reading bounded content. Remove legacy-cli/ARCMUX_GOAL_BIN execution from daemon summarization entirely. Use an explicit direct-API provider, two fixed workers, bounded admission, per-session queued/active dedupe, and a persistent per-turn attempt ledger with permanent/transient classification. Route manual summarize through the same safe execution boundary and make it the explicit attempt-reset surface. Embed build revision/safety metadata and require installed-binary attestation before production restart.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No automatic or on-demand daemon summarization code can execute Grok, Codex, Claude, a browser, or any external agent CLI; legacy-cli and ARCMUX_GOAL_BIN are rejected/ignored fail-closed. 2. With no explicit direct API provider, missing/unsafe key files, or HTTP 401/403, summarization performs zero subprocesses, admits no retry storm, and records a permanent per-turn terminal result. 3. Each session turn receives at most 3 total automatic attempts across daemon restarts; transient failures back off, exhausted turns stay terminal, a new turn resets the key, and an explicit POST /session/summarize request may reset that turn once. 4. Input comes only from the exact frontmatter-verified turn_contract.canonical_history binding under the configured history root; legacy vault_link, pane scrollback, cwd/host/mtime search, symlinks, duplicate conversation IDs, and stale/mismatched bindings fail closed. 5. One process-wide fixed worker pool runs at most 2 summaries concurrently with a bounded queue, per-session queued/active deduplication, and observable drop/backlog behavior; a regression corpus of hundreds cannot create unbounded goroutines or work. 6. Automatic and on-demand summarization share the same provider, validation, attempt, and concurrency boundary; feature extraction remains bounded and sanitized. 7. Logs expose only safe session ID, canonical-history basename, turn key, attempt, queue state, and failure class; no prompts, transcript text, model output, credentials, or full paths. 8. The binary reports build revision and a summarizer safety capability; install/release verification refuses to treat a stale or unsafe artifact as restartable. 9. Focused race/load/auth/history tests, full Go tests, vet/static checks, build, and an isolated real-binary E2E pass while production remains inactive and disabled.

Incident contained 2026-07-26 14:20:51 PT: arcmux stopped, 337 remaining arcmux-overall-goal Grok children killed. Observed >380 Grok processes, 14,598 cgroup tasks, 23.9 GiB resident and 55.9 GiB peak. Existing main is ahead 4/behind 54; preserve stash concurrent-exec-gc-WIP.

Recurrence 2026-07-30 10:31:22 PT: service had been restarted at 2026-07-26 14:55:55 PT with /home/blin/.local/bin/arcmux mtime 2026-07-16 11:36:29 PT. Binary lacks the post-build hardening markers (ARCMUX_GOAL_PROVIDER, direct OpenAI endpoint, bounded current_work log strings); no ARCMUX_GOAL_*/provider credentials exist in the service environment and [current_work] is empty. Therefore the pre-hardening resolver auto-selected grok from PATH. Old scheduler uses host+CWD newest-history correlation plus a 60s timestamp retry but no active single-flight/global cap: 508 retained prompt files arrived over 89.661s, 507 byte-identical, consistent with repeated waves across many stale managed sessions. Observed 508 Grok + 508 Chrome, 12,210 cgroup tasks, 10.5 GiB current and 111.4 GiB peak; Chrome command targeted accounts.x.ai/oauth2/device. Containment: SIGSTOP PID 1888, exact-name process cleanup, then clean systemctl --user stop; all arcmux/Grok/Chrome processes are zero, tmux sessions survived due KillMode=process. arcmux.service disabled to prevent login/reboot recurrence. Keep inactive/disabled until arcmux-xev acceptance criteria pass and a validated binary is deployed.

Root and profile daemons use separate hook-state/raw-output namespaces for duplicate IDs and share one process-wide two-slot inference pool, while retaining per-session single-flight. title: Linux service path never enables the systemd user unit — arcmux dies at reboot
description:
Observed 2026-09-10: labs booted 2026-09-09 23:31 with no arcmux running; last daemon log was Aug 12. The unit was loaded but 'disabled', so nothing started it at boot.

Root cause: the Makefile Linux path only ever calls 'systemctl --user start/restart', never 'enable'.
- make start  -> systemctl --user start   (runs now, not at boot)
- service-install refresh path -> systemctl --user restart (same)

macOS is boot-durable: packaging/launchd/com.blin.arcmux.plist sets RunAtLoad+KeepAlive and 'make start' uses launchctl bootstrap, which persists in the login domain. The plist comment claims RunAtLoad is 'the macOS analogue of the systemd Restart=always unit on labs', but Restart=always only covers crashes, not boot — so the documented parity does not hold.

Fix: use 'systemctl --user enable --now' in start, and ensure enablement in the service-install was_active refresh path, so an already-running-but-disabled deploy heals itself.
close_reason: Fixed: make start now uses 'enable --now'; service-install enables an already-active unit before restarting. Labs enabled by hand and running (PID 1126366, 23 sessions restored).

title: Supervise durable mesh peer endpoints
description: The multi-peer protocol is released, but the current devbox/labs reachability depends on temporary SSH loopback forwards outside arcmux. Native Tailscale endpoints remain preferred when operator authorization and tailnet topology permit; otherwise arcmux must own a narrowly structured, durable SSH-tunnel fallback so an endpoint is recreated after Wi-Fi/VPN or transport-process loss without weakening the loopback-only mesh listener.
design: Keep the mesh listener loopback-only. Prefer direct ws:// tailnet endpoints. For unreachable cross-tailnet peers, support an optional per-peer structured SSH local-forward transport in the owner-only mesh registry (target + loopback local/remote endpoints; no arbitrary shell command). The mesh manager supervises one independent child process per configured peer with bounded jittered backoff, context-bound shutdown, safe status, and hot-reload/daemon-restart recreation. Peer tokens remain registry-only and must be redacted from every surfaced error/log.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Native Tailscale Serve remains supported/preferred when authorization and tailnet topology permit; a managed SSH tunnel is an accepted durable fallback. 2. Killing a managed tunnel process causes arcmux to recreate it automatically with bounded exponential backoff and without manual stale control-socket or temp-file cleanup. 3. An unreachable host backs off without busy-looping, while devbox and labs supervisors and mesh connections operate independently. 4. Daemon restart recreates configured transports; daemon stop/hot reload terminates only arcmux-owned tunnel processes and never local agent sessions. 5. Loopback listener safety remains enforced and tunnel local/remote endpoints are loopback-only; no arbitrary shell execution surface is introduced. 6. Tokens/invites and any secret-bearing failure text never appear in status, logs, shell history, or task notes. 7. Focused unit/race tests cover process death/restart, unreachable host backoff, two-peer independence, daemon restart, and secret-safe status/logging. 8. Live dogfood shows ref simultaneously restores devbox and labs after tunnel-process death and daemon restart with no manual process cleanup, then removes the old temporary /tmp tunnel configs/processes.
notes:
Implementation is complete on codex/mesh-transport-supervisor-20260716. Initial commit 00971c7 added structured per-peer SSH local-forward supervision and authoritative `arcmux info --json` device_id. title: Probe and reconnect multiple mesh peers independently
description: Support multiple configured peers such as devbox and labs. design: Keep one connector goroutine per outbound peer. Before every WebSocket reconnect, run a portable <=1s TCP probe. Model retry cause explicitly: probe_failure and connection_drop use full-jitter bounds [reconnect_min, min(reconnect_max, max(reconnect_min, 5s))]; handshake_failure after a successful probe retains [reconnect_min, reconnect_max]. A deterministic retry-delay seam defaults to fullJitter and exists so high-attempt network lifecycle tests can prove the selected production bounds without wall-clock sleeps. title: Exec session/process GC: exited one-shot exec handles pile up in agent list + hung codex exec subprocesses never reaped
description:
Two related leaks in internal/daemon/exec_transport.go + daemon.go.

LEAK 1 (visible in voxtop Agents tab, IMG_6211): one-shot AutoClose exec sessions (arcmux-cli exec without --keep) set StateExited on completion (waitExecPrompt) but are NEVER removed from d.sessions. persistSessions() only excludes terminal sessions from the on-disk file (so they clear only on daemon restart); ListSessions() returns the full in-memory map unfiltered; HTTP /sessions (handleSessionsList) and gRPC ListSessions return them -> voxtop shows piles of codex_exec-* / claude_exec-* marked 'Exited' (22m, 28m, 35m, 1h old) with live call buttons. Class-agnostic (codex AND claude).

LEAK 2 (hung subprocesses): exec subprocess built with exec.Command (no ctx binding), no Setpgid/process group; runCtx/monitor cancel is a no-op for the process; no daemon-side watchdog/timeout; client disconnect/timeout (arcmux-cli exec ctx) and daemon Stop() both orphan the process instead of killing it; killExecSession's proc.Kill() reaps only the node wrapper, orphaning the rust grandchild. Result: codex exec children stuck >3min as live children of the daemon, plus orphans after restarts.

FIX: (1) hide terminal AutoClose sessions from list views + reaper goroutine deletes them from d.sessions after a short grace (preserve the Capture-by-id window arcmux-cli exec needs); (2) Setpgid on exec cmds + watchdog that kills the process group on runCtx/request-ctx cancel + group-kill in killExecSession + optional daemon-side max-runtime watchdog; wire daemon Stop() to actually kill tracked exec process groups.

title: Implement safe cross-device agent handoff
description: Make it easy to pause an agent conversation on one device and resume it on another using the mesh plus already-synced history, branches, and stored artifacts. Handoff must be explicit, inspectable, and safe when working trees or credentials are not transferable.
design: Build on the remote-session/artifact protocol, not terminal scraping. Use a declarative handoff manifest and two-phase prepare/accept acknowledgement. Never infer or silently copy credentials. Prefer synced history plus pushed branches; allow an explicit patch/bundle artifact as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The source produces a versioned handoff manifest containing trace/session lineage, latest user goal, conversation-history reference, repo/branch/head, worktree cleanliness, artifact references, validation state, and target device. 2. The target validates repo/artifact availability, creates or reuses the correct worktree, starts a supervised agent with inherited trace context, and records source/target lineage. 4. Repeated handoff requests are idempotent and never spawn duplicate continuations. 5. Failed or offline targets leave the source session intact and a retryable request queued. 6. Tests cover clean branch, stored patch, missing history, dirty unexported state, offline target, duplicate delivery, and successful laptop-to-devbox/labs resume.

title: Browser E2E: make restart converges to one daemon
description:
## Summary
Browser E2E coverage has observed occasional double-spawn behavior after restart. The scoped restart path is `make restart`: after it completes and settles, process state should converge to exactly one daemon instance.

## Expected behavior
Running `make restart` repeatedly leaves one daemon running, with no duplicate process surviving from the previous run or appearing during restart convergence.

## Scope
This is specifically about `make restart`, not browser reloads, test runner retries, manual daemon restarts, or service container restarts.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] No duplicate daemon process remains after restart convergence

title: make restart leaves exactly one daemon
description:
When `make restart` is used, the restart path can leave a duplicate daemon behind. Only one process binds the listening port, but an extra daemon remains running, making process state ambiguous after restart.

Expected behavior: `make restart` is idempotent and collapses the process set to exactly one daemon.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Running `make restart` while a daemon is already running leaves exactly one daemon process.
- [ ] Only the surviving daemon owns the listening port.
- [ ] No duplicate or stale daemon process remains after restart completes.
- [ ] Repeating `make restart` multiple times preserves the one-daemon invariant.
